title: Renewal Decision Lab — 60m Sprint Agenda & Action Backlog
content:
Purpose: Run a focused 60-minute decision lab with the customer to (1) surface blocker risks to renewal, (2) agree on next-step commitments, and (3) leave with a shared 30/60/90 action backlog and owner map. This is intentionally compact — use for mid-track renewals where the relationship exists but there are open questions or a weak renewal signal.

Quick notes to facilitator (tone + setup):
- Keep it outcome-oriented: aim for 3 concrete commitments with owners and dates.
- Neutral framing: ‘we’re here to align and reduce blockers’ rather than pressure for a yes/no.
- Time-box and call out explicit parking-lot items.
- Bring one data chart (usage + error rate trend) and one customer story (impact snapshot).
- If execs present, focus on decisions they can influence; defer tactical items to follow-ups.

Pre-meeting (send ~3 business days ahead):
- Invite email (subject line): "Renewal Decision Lab — 60m — Pre-reads + Goal". Include: agenda, 1-page health snapshot, ask for any critical topics they want on the table.
- Pre-read pack (attach):
  - 1-page adoption snapshot (MAU / active routes / top 3 models used)
  - Latency & error trend (30/90 day)
  - Billing vs committed capacity (variance + forecast)
  - Open support/ticket summary (tickets open > 7d)
  - Proposed renewal timeline (dates + options)
- Ask customer to confirm decision-makers for renewal and any procurement/legal blockers.
- Internal prep: sync with Solutions Eng 24–48h ahead to confirm technical owners and one escalation path.

60 Minute Sprint Agenda (time-boxed):
0–5m | Welcome + Objective (Facilitator)
  - Quick round: attendees + decision role (Decision Maker / Influencer / Technical SME).
  - State goal: leave with 3 commitments and next checkpoint.

5–18m | Health Snapshot (Owner: CSM)
  - Present the 1-page pre-read highlights (usage, latency, costs).
  - One positive impact story (recent win).
  - Quick customer reaction: 2 mins of open comments.

18–33m | Risk Radar + Root Cause Triage (Facilitator + Tech SME)
  - Show top 4 risks (adoption, cost, reliability, procurement). Each risk 3 bullets and current evidence.
  - For each risk: ask customer to score (0–5) perceived severity and likelihood. Capture scores in chat.
  - Triage one high-risk item immediately if it blocks renewal (5–10m deep dive).

33–45m | Options & Tradeoffs (Facilitator + CSM)
  - Present 3 realistic renewal options (e.g., renew-as-is, limited pilot + bridge discount, or extend with SLA uplift).
  - Walk tradeoffs: timeline, cost delta, technical lift, ROI.
  - Ask customer to indicate preferred option (poll).

45–55m | Commitment Ledger (Facilitator — live doc)
  - Agree on 3 commitments: owner, deliverable, target date. Example categories: procurement milestone, reliability remediation, new integration checkpoint.
  - Capture any follow-ups that need more detail in the 30/60/90 backlog.

55–60m | Close: Next Checkpoint & Escalation Path (Facilitator)
  - Confirm date/time for the 30-minute checkpoint (within 10 business days).
  - Reiterate escalation contact (SE lead + CSM).
  - Quick poll: confidence level (green/amber/red).

Facilitation script snippets (short, usable lines):
- Opening: "Thanks all — our goal for the next hour is to identify the minimum set of things that need to happen so everyone can make a decision confidently."
- When stuck: "Let's park the deep technical steps and agree on the decision we can make today — we'll capture the technical action and owner for the follow-up."
- When scope creeps: "This is a great idea, but to keep today's meeting outcome-oriented we'll add this to the 30/60/90 backlog and assign an owner."
- When execs ask for alternatives: "We have three options prepared — would you prefer we walk through them or do you want an off-line cost modeling session with procurement after this call?"

Decision scoring rubric (use during Risk Radar):
- Severity (0–5): 0 = negligible impact; 5 = blocks business outcome/production.
- Likelihood (0–5): 0 = won't happen; 5 = very likely within 30 days.
- Priority = Severity x Likelihood (capture 0–25). Discuss items >12 immediately.

30/60/90 Backlog template (one-line per item, captured live):
- ID | Short title | Owner (name + role) | Due date | Acceptance criteria | Status (todo/in-progress/blocker)
  - Example: CSB-1 | Reduce inference errors on route X | Jordan Reed (SE) | 2025-01-28 | errors < 0.5% on 24h rolling | in-progress

Pre-flight checklist for facilitator (day-of):
- Confirm meeting link + recording enabled.
- Post pre-read in chat and Slack channel.
- Confirm SE & billing rep can join for technical/contract questions.
- Bring live doc template and set up initial Commitment Ledger rows.
- Print quick notes on top 3 co-sell/partner steps if applicable.

Follow-up email template (send within 24h):
Subject: "Notes + Commitments — Renewal Decision Lab (Company X)"
Hi <CustomerLead>,
Thanks again for joining — attached are the one-page health snapshot and the live Commitment Ledger. Per our discussion, three agreed commitments: (1) <owner> will <deliverable> by <date>, (2) <owner> will <deliverable> by <date>, (3) <owner> will <deliverable> by <date>.
Next: 30-minute checkpoint on <date/time> to validate progress. If anything shifts please let us know and we'll reschedule.
Best,
Emily (CSM)

Facilitator escalation ladder (internal):
- Level 1: CSM (Emily Zhang) — triage & scope.
- Level 2: Solutions Eng Lead (Samir Patel) — technical unblock.
- Level 3: Head of Customer Success (Laura Mendes) — commercial/contract escalation.

Quick heuristics & guardrails (notes to self):
- If renewal confidence is red after the meeting, propose a 14-day tactical war room with daily 15m syncs.
- Avoid detailed procurement/legal negotiations during the 60m slot; capture and escalate.
- Use the Decision Scoring to force prioritization — customers often treat all issues as equally urgent.

Appendix: sample health snapshot sections (one-pagers to attach)
1) Usage & Adoption: top routes, active keys, trend lines. One-sentence takeaway.
2) Reliability: 30/90d latency P50/P95 and error rate. Include any incident recency notes.
3) Cost & Contract: current bill vs committed capacity, forecast to renewal date, recommended options.
4) Open risks & tickets: list with age and owner.

Parking lot & research items (post-meeting):
- Numbered list captured live and assigned for the 30-day backlog.

— end of draft —
Notes: want a condensed slide deck (3 slides) to live-share: 1) health snapshot, 2) risk radar with scores, 3) commitment ledger. Create slide deck template and add link to this doc.
